claims.claim: Sendbird publishes no OpenAPI document; the contract is deterministically reconstructed from the pinned official generated SDK
claims.summary: The official SDK repository is the machine-readable representation of the Platform API v3 wire contract (83 REST/JSON request methods over 11 generated API classes); the reconstructed OpenAPI 3.1 document is retained as evidence in the metadata repository and is reproducible via scripts/reconstruct-sendbird-oas.mjs.

claims.claim: The client connects directly to `https://api-{app_id}.sendbird.com` with the caller's own application credentials
claims.summary: The SDK base server configuration uses https://api-{app_id}.sendbird.com with /v3 path prefixes and api-token header authentication; the official overview describes the Platform API as a REST/JSON server-side API.

claims.claim: Every request requires the caller's Sendbird application ID (base-URL host) and Application API Token (`api-token` header).
claims.summary: All 83 generated SDK request methods set the api-token (or Api-Token) header; the reconstructed contract models this as an apiKey security scheme and the SDK/CLI attach the header only when SENDBIRD_API_TOKEN or the apiToken option is configured.

claims.claim: all Hub copy is independently authored.
claims.summary: The TypeScript package.json declares the Unlicense and the Java SDK ships an MIT LICENSE.md (Copyright (c) 2022 Sendbird), permitting use of the SDK interface contract; the metadata product does not redistribute official documentation prose or SDK source.

claims.claim: Pontx Hub does not proxy, cache, or aggregate Sendbird application data.
claims.summary: The product provenance sets riskReview.hubProxyEnabled=false and every endpoint disables Hub execution; the SDK/CLI connect directly at the caller's direction with the caller's own application credentials, and the product Skill instructs preview-first mutation confirmation.
